findings.body: The old Bash runner reported a timeout as `timed out after ${per_file_timeout}s`, which gave "timed out after 300s" by default. The new message is `f'timed out after {timeout}'`, so a timeout with the default value of `300` now reads "timed out after 300" with no unit, in the summary, the step summary and the `::error` annotation. The new error annotation also drops the `web/` prefix and the "open its log group above" hint. This only affects how results are reported; pass/fail is unchanged. A possible fix is to append `s` when the value has no suffix.
findings.title: Timeout reason no longer shows the default unit

overall_explanation:
I read every diff page of all 6 changed files.

**CI build change:** CI now runs `npm run build:bundle` instead of `npm run build`. This is safe. `web/tsconfig.json` sets `noEmit: true`, so the skipped `tsc -b` produced no files that Vite needs, and the separate `npm run typecheck` step still runs before the build. Local `npm run build` still runs `tsc -b` first and then the same bundle command.

**New runner:** the Python runner `web_tests.py` behaves like the old Bash loop:
- It runs from `web/` and keeps the same `timeout --kill-after=10` / `node --max-old-space-size=2048 --experimental-strip-types` command.
- It discovers `tools/*.test.mjs` the same way, runs every file even after failures, and exits nonzero if any file fails.
- It writes the same step summary and keeps the log groups balanced.

It also adds cleanup:
- It kills each test's process group after the test exits.
- On SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP it cleans up and exits with 128 + the signal number.
- It rejects bad `WEB_TEST_JOBS` and `WEB_TEST_TIMEOUT` values.

The old retry list was already empty, so removing it changes nothing.

**Tests:** the new unittest file is picked up by the existing "CI script tests" step (`unittest discover --start-directory .github/scripts`). Its fixtures (a fake `node` on `PATH`, plus GNU `timeout` and `/proc`) look consistent with what the runner does.

**Remaining issue:** one minor reporting regression in how timeouts are described (see the finding).
